title: Swimmer drowning at Fountainstown Beach
description: A swimmer got into difficulty in rough surf conditions. RNLI Crosshaven lifeboat launched and recovered casualty. Inquest returned a verdict of accidental drowning. Conditions: elevated swell from Storm Nadine remnants, onshore SW wind 18-22kts, spring tide.

title: Two swimmers rescued off Fountainstown
description: Two adults rescued after being caught in a rip current. Conditions: W wind 15kts, 1.5m swell, neap tide. Saved by RNLI Crosshaven ILB.

title: Inflatable lilo blown offshore from Fountainstown
description: RNLI Crosshaven launched at 14:52 after inflatables and lilos drifted from Fountainstown in a force 5–6 offshore wind. Crew recovered the inflatable at Ringabella beach; users had already made it ashore. Patsy Fegan (RNLI Ops Manager): 'with a force 5 wind they could have drifted well offshore.'

title: Kayaker in difficulty Fountainstown
description: Kayaker capsized in unexpectedly strong tidal flow near headland. Rescued by passing boat. SSW wind 12kts, low swell.

title: Father and son swept out at Fountainstown
description: A nine-year-old boy on an inflatable was swept out in a strong current at Fountainstown at approximately 19:30. His father swam out to help; the boy made it back with a kayaker's help but the father was left clinging to a marker buoy. Five teenagers in a RIB reached him before the lifeboat and brought him safely to shore. Coast Guard and RNLI Crosshaven also responded.

title: Child swept from rocks Fountainstown
description: Child swept from rocks by unexpected wave surge. Recovered safely. High spring tide, swell 1.8m, calm wind — deceptive calm with ocean swell.

title: Child fatally swept into sea at Fountainstown
description: A 7-year-old girl was swept into the sea by a large wave at approximately 16:40. Sea conditions were choppy. An extensive search involving RNLI Crosshaven, Shannon Coast Guard helicopter, Gardaí and fire services recovered her body near the shore at approximately 19:45. Inquest verdict: accidental drowning.
